name: Tom Shows Disapproval to Bacon with a Facial Expression
description: Tom raises his eyebrows and frowns at Bacon.
related_events: Tom expresses disapproval to Bacon through facial expression

name: Ed Stands Outside JD's and Walks Away
description: Ed, his face shadowed by a two-day stubble and his eyes sunken into dark sockets, stumbles down the street with a bottle of scotch protruding from his pocket. He comes to a stop in front of JD's, stares at the entrance, then turns and walks away without going in.
related_events: Ed decides not to enter JD's

name: Don's Ejection and Outburst on the Street
description: Don was thrown out onto the street. As soon as he hit the pavement, he began screaming and cursing loudly, his voice filled with rage and anguish.
related_events: Don is ejected onto the street and begins screaming and cursing

name: Barrv Enters the Information
description: Barrv sighs with relief and begins typing. His fingers move across the keyboard as he inputs the necessary details. The screen updates with the completed fields.
related_events: Barrv types in the relevant information

name: Reveal the Stash and Shock Ed
description: An off-screen voice speaks, saying they must have someone sensible involved if they’re holding a container full of cash in shoeboxes and a skip-load of Class A drugs. On the word 'cash,' Ed’s head, previously slumped at a pitiful angle, snaps upright. His dark eyes widen sharply, fixed on the source of the voice, his expression frozen in shock.
related_events: Character reveals presence of large cash and drug stash
Ed reacts with sudden shock to new information

name: Barry Answers the Ringing Phone
description: Barry's phone rings suddenly. He jumps, startled, and fumbles to find it. He pulls it out and answers, saying, 'What?'
related_events: Barry's phone rings startling him
Barry answers his ringing phone

name: Eddy Sets High Stakes, Hatchet Acts Suspicious
description: Eddy places a ten-thousand-dollar blind bet, signaling the start of the poker round. Across the table, Hatchet runs a hand down his leg, his eyes darting, posture tense. The room grows quiet, the air thick with anticipation.
related_events: Eddy announces ten thousand dollar blind bet
Hatchet feels his leg and appears suspicious

name: Dog Distributes Money and Pills While Confronting Plank
description: Dog stands over a small pile of money and pills, handing out portions to his associates. He turns to Plank and speaks firmly, telling him that if he finds a job worth doing, his share will improve. He asks if Plank has a problem with that. Plank does not respond.
related_events: Dog distributes money and pills to his associates
Dog lectures Plank about job performance and reward

name: Discussion About Known Contacts
description: The back of a head is visible. One man asks another if he knows certain people well. The second man replies that he’s been buying gear from one of them for a couple of years. The first man asks what they’re like. The second man says they’re poofs, nothing heavy—four public school guys, soft as shite.
related_events: Character inquires about familiarity with individuals
Character reveals history of purchasing gear
Character describes individuals as unimpressive and effeminate

name: Bacon Responds to SOAP's Challenge
description: SOAP demanded that Bacon come up with a suggestion, questioning his intelligence. Bacon replied that he was thinking, that he was still working on it.
related_events: SOAP challenges Bacon to offer a suggestion
Bacon asserts he is in the process of thinking

name: Big Chris and Little Chris Observe a Suspicious Man
description: Big Chris asked how long the man had been there. Little Chris replied that it had been about twenty minutes. Big Chris wanted to know if the man was alone. Little Chris said he was, and that he was just carrying a bag. Big Chris suggested they take a look together.
related_events: Big Chris inquires about Little Chris's observation of a man
Little Chris reports details about a man's presence and belongings
Big Chris proposes joint inspection of the man's activity

name: Hatchet Harry Confronts Smithy Robinson
description: Hatchet Harry invited Smithy Robinson to his place to address rumors that Smithy was on the take. Smithy arrived and attempted to explain himself, but his response was unsatisfactory. Within a minute, Harry lost his temper. He grabbed a fifteen-inch black rubber cock, the nearest object at hand, and used it to beat Smithy to death.
related_events: Harry invites Smithy Robinson for an explanation
Smithy Robinson fails to adequately explain himself
Harry loses temper and attacks Smithy Robinson

name: Soap Presents a Fundraising Idea
description: Soap finishes explaining his fundraising proposal and tells the others they can keep all the money. Bacon and Tom frown at him in silence. Tom then responds sharply, saying he's heard many stupid ideas, but Soap's makes Bacon's idea seem inspired.
related_events: Soap proposes a fundraising idea
Bacon and Tom react negatively to Soap's idea
Tom criticizes Soap's idea as absurd

name: Arrive Home and Go Inside Without Acknowledging Each Other
description: Ed, Bacon, Soap, and Tom pulled up and parked outside their house. As they got out, they passed Plank and John, who had just parked nearby. No one spoke or looked at one another. The two groups moved past each other in silence, then went to separate doors and went inside.
related_events: Group parks cars outside their house
Characters pass each other without acknowledgment
Characters head to separate doors after arriving

name: Hatchet on the Phone While Eddy and Friends Listen In
description: Hatchet sits behind a large antique desk cluttered with weapons, his hand resting on a shotgun. He speaks into the phone, his voice tense, as the hatchet stands embedded in a block of wood nearby. On one side of a split screen, Eddy and his friends listen silently, their faces lit by the glow of a monitor. The camera holds on both sides of the exchange, the room behind Hatchet lined with shotguns, while the others remain hidden, watching and waiting.
related_events: Hatchet speaks on phone while touching shotgun
Split screen shows Eddy and friends eavesdropping
Hatchet sits behind antique desk with weapons displayed

name: Hatchet Folds, Eddy Reacts with Caution
description: Hatchet pauses, then announces, 'I'll fold.' A ripple of surprise passes through the onlookers. Eddy frowns slightly, his expression darkening. Without a word, he glances discreetly over his shoulder, scanning the area. Once satisfied, he reaches forward and gathers the pile of winnings toward himself, saying, 'Don't go spending that all at once, boy.'
related_events: Hatchet decides to fold in the card game
Eddy expresses concern over Hatchet's decision
Eddy checks his surroundings for potential threats
Eddy collects the winnings from the card game

name: Dean and Gary Argue Over the Disguise
description: The Scousers entered the large house, moving quietly through the rooms. Dean glanced at Gary’s disguise and frowned. The stocking covered only half his face, and a frilly artificial moustache clung to his upper lip, failing to look threatening. A neatly styled bouffant sat perfectly in place on his head. 'Can't you pull that stocking down further, Kenny?' Dean asked. Gary smoothed his hair with both hands. 'It just cost me fifty quid to have this done,' he said. 'If you think I am going to ruin it for a couple of old bastards you're mistaken, Kenny.'
related_events: Scousers enter and move through large house
Dean expresses distaste for Gary's disguise
Dean requests Gary to adjust stocking over face
Gary refuses to adjust disguise to protect hairstyle

name: Tom and JD Confront Ed About the Card Game
description: Tom, Soap, and Bacon are in the bar, stunned to see Ed walk in. Tom points to his watch and snaps at Ed, demanding to know why he’s there instead of resting. He reminds him he’s supposed to be preparing for a card game with Hatchet Harry. Ed grimaces as his father, JD, steps forward and asks directly if he’s playing cards tonight with Harry. Ed hesitates, then denies it, saying it’s a silly idea and he wouldn’t have anything to do with it.
related_events: Tom expresses disbelief at Ed's presence in the bar
Tom reminds Ed of his card game obligation with Hatchet Harry
Ed grimaces as his father confronts him about the card game
Ed denies any involvement in a card game with Hatchet Harry

name: Boys witness burning man fleeing Samoan Jo's
description: As the boys approached Samoan Jo's, a man burst out of the door, his body covered in flames. He ran wildly, arms flailing, while his friends rushed after him, slapping at the fire and trying to smother it. The boys stood still, eyes wide, taking in the scene with mild shock. Tom glanced at the others and said, 'I heard this place was rough.'
related_events: Man runs out of Samoan Jo's covered in flames
Friends attempt to extinguish flames on man
Boys react with mild shock to burning man
Tom comments on Samoan Jo's being rough

name: J and Charles Confront Unexpected Visitor at Illegal Forest Site
description: J and Charles stand in a small, humid, artificially lit forest, each wearing lab coats with long hair and small goatees, smoking a joint. J coughs and remarks on the weight of the gear, saying he suspects they should have been rocket scientists or Nobel Peace Prize winners. Suddenly, a horn blares—the doorbell. Charles turns sharply, eyes widening, and asks who the hell is at the door.
related_events: J and Charles smoke a joint in an illegal forest cultivation site
J expresses doubt about their career path while feeling the weight of equipment
Doorbell horn sounds at the illegal forest site
Charles reacts to unexpected visitor at the door

name: Eddy Bets Twenty Thousand with a Running Flush
description: Eddy looks at his cards and sees a running flush. He pushes twenty thousand into the pot.
related_events: Eddy places a twenty thousand bet with a running flush

name: Barry Zooms In But Sees Nothing
description: Barry adjusts the zoom, leaning in closer to get a clearer view. The lens focuses, but the image remains empty. He sees nothing.
related_events: Barry attempts to get a better view by zooming in

name: Ed Takes the Lead in the Game
description: Music begins as a montage unfolds, showing Ed, Hatchet, and Barry at work. Ed pulls ahead in the game, building a lead of around 250,000. Pieces of paper are signed, and IOUs begin to change hands as the game grows more intense.
related_events: Music begins playing at the start of the scene
Montage shows Ed, Hatchet and Barry engaged in work activities
Ed accumulates a large lead in the game

name: Ed, Hatchet, and Barry Sign IOUs as the Game Spirals
description: Music starts. The scene cuts to a montage of Ed, Hatchet, and Barry deep in the game. Ed is up by 250,000, but the pace has intensified. Bets grow larger, hands move quickly, and pieces of paper begin to change hands. IOUs are scribbled and signed, passed between them without hesitation. The table fills with handwritten notes, each representing a debt, piling up as the game surges beyond its original limits.
related_events: Game escalates out of control with IOUs being signed

name: Nick and Tom Move Through a Maze of Boxes
description: Nick and Tom make their way through a cluttered storage area filled with stacked boxes. Nick pauses briefly to examine one of the boxes, running his fingers over it with interest. He turns to Tom and asks how much it costs. Tom replies that Nick already knows the price. Nick asks again, clarifying whether the price includes the amplifier. Tom insists it does not.
related_events: Nick and Tom navigate through a maze of boxes

name: Nick and Tom Discuss the Price of a Box and Amplifier
description: Nick runs his fingers over one of the boxes, turning to Tom. "How much did you say it was, Tom?" Tom replies, "You know how much it is, Nick." Nick glances back at the box. "And that does include the amp?" Tom shakes his head. "You know it doesn't include the amp."
related_events: Nick inquires about the price of a box
Tom confirms Nick already knows the price
Nick asks if the amplifier is included in the price
Tom states the amplifier is not included

name: Ed's Hidden Alertness
description: Ed sits in an armchair, dressed neatly, his face still and eyes closed as a cool track plays. The camera glides slowly down his body, coming to rest on his hand. There, he is deftly cutting a pack with precision. A knock sounds at the door. His eyes snap open.
related_events: Ed sits motionless with eyes closed while music plays
Camera reveals Ed skillfully cutting a pack with his hand

name: Ed Reacts to a Door Knock
description: A knock sounds at the door. Ed, seated in an armchair with his eyes closed, instantly opens his eyes.
related_events: Someone knocks on Ed's door
Ed opens his eyes after hearing a knock

name: Ed Returns Home and Collapses
description: Ed fumbles with his keys at the front door before finally getting inside. He moves through the entryway in a daze, takes off his jacket, and opens the cupboard doors. He hangs his coat on a hanger, but it slips off and falls to the floor. Ed sinks down and collapses in a heap.
related_events: Ed struggles to unlock and enter his front door
Ed removes his jacket and opens cupboard doors
Ed's coat falls off the hanger after being hung
Ed collapses in a pile on the floor

name: Ed overhears neighbors criticizing hippies and their cannabis business
description: Ed fumbles with his keys at his front door and enters his house in a daze. He takes off his jacket and opens the cupboard doors. As he hangs his coat, it slips off the hanger and falls to the floor. He collapses into a heap. With the cupboard doors now open, the sound from next door carries clearly. Voices drift through, speaking about people who wear funny hippie clothes and talk nonsense. They say the only thing those people are good at is growing weed, and that the business has grown too big for them to handle.
related_events: Ed overhears neighbors' conversation through open cupboard doors
Neighbors criticize hippie lifestyle and cannabis business growth

name: Winston Confronts Willy and Charlie Over Unlocked Cage
description: The door opens and Willy steps in, carrying two large bags of fertilizer under his arms. He asks Charlie for help, saying he might break a sweat any second. From the top of the stairs, Winston calls out, asking why the security cage is open. Charlie shrugs and says it’s for security. Winston replies that the point of having the cage is to use it. Charlie explains that he let Willy in because Willy lives there. Winston insists that Charlie didn’t know it was Willy at first. Willy tells Winston to calm down, pointing out that Charlie recognized him. Winston responds that both Charlie and Willy are slow to react in critical moments and orders them to keep the cage locked. He then notices the bags Willy is holding and asks what’s inside. Willy says it’s fertilizer. Winston reminds him that he was supposed to buy a money counter six hours ago. Willy argues they need the fertilizer. Winston shouts that they also need the money counter and that he refuses to count the money by hand. He adds that if Willy had to buy fertilizer, he should have been more discreet, especially since they grow large amounts of cannabis and Willy doesn’t look like an ordinary gardener. Without waiting for a reply, Winston turns and walks away.
related_events: Willy arrives with bags of fertilizer
Winston reprimands Willy and Charlie for security lapse
Winston questions the purpose of the security cage
Charlie defends leaving the cage unlocked

name: Winston Confronts Willy Over Fertilizer and Missing Money Counter
description: The door opens and Willy enters carrying two large bags of fertilizer under his arms. Charlie hesitates before helping him. From the top of the stairs, Winston calls out, asking why the security cage is open. Charlie shrugs and says it’s for security, but Winston snaps back that the point of having it is to use it. Charlie explains that he let Willy in because Willy lives there. Winston argues that Charlie didn’t know it was Willy until he saw him. Willy tries to calm him, saying there’s no issue since Charlie recognized him. Winston ignores the comment and asks what Willy is carrying. Willy says it’s fertilizer. Winston reminds him that he sent him out six hours ago to buy a money counter, not fertilizer. He grows angry, pointing out they need to get the money out by Thursday and that no one will count it by hand. He also scolds Willy for being careless—buying large amounts of fertilizer makes them look suspicious, especially since they grow cannabis and Willy doesn’t blend in as a typical gardener. Without waiting for a reply, Winston turns and walks away, leaving Willy and Charlie standing in the doorway.
related_events: Winston confronts Willy about returning with fertilizer instead of a money counter
Winston criticizes Willy for lack of subtlety in purchasing fertilizer
Winston storms off after confrontation with Willy

name: Tom and Nick Banter About Tom's Thinness
description: Tom stands in the grocer's shop talking with Nick the Greek. Tom gestures to his midriff and looks puzzled. Nick remarks on Tom's thinness, and Tom responds with a confused expression, inviting both Nick and the newly arrived Eddy to join him in his orifice. The exchange carries a playful tone.
related_events: Tom engages in conversation with Nick the Greek

name: Eddy Arrives at the Grocer's Shop
description: Eddy walks into the grocer's shop and greets Nick the Greek. Tom is already there, speaking with Nick. Eddy steps into the conversation, joining the two men. Tom looks down at his stomach and makes a confused face. "Please, both join me in my orifice," he says.
related_events: Eddy arrives at the grocer's shop
Eddy greets Nick the Greek and joins the conversation

name: Tom Examines His Midriff and Invites Others Into His Orifice
description: Eddy arrives at a grocer's shop and greets Nick the Greek, who is speaking with Tom. When Eddy asks Tom what he has been eating, Tom looks down at his midriff with a puzzled expression. After a moment, he says, 'Please, both join me in my orifice.'
related_events: Tom examines his midriff and shows confusion
Tom makes a surreal invitation involving his orifice

name: Eddy and the Doorman at the Card Game
description: Eddy and his friends arrive at the venue and are met by a doorman who blocks their entry. The doorman asks for invitations. Eddy asks what invitations are, and the doorman explains they are white pieces of paper with their names on them. Eddy replies that he has about a hundred thousand pieces of paper with the Queen on them and asks if that will work. The doorman tells him only he can enter, and the others must wait at Samoan Jo's next door. Eddy questions whether Samoan Jo's is the pub, but the doorman insists no one without an invitation is allowed inside, and only card players are permitted that night.
related_events: Eddy and his friends arrive at the venue and are stopped by the doorman
Doorman demands invitations from Eddy and his group
Eddy offers currency as an alternative to an invitation

name: Eddy Gains Entry, Friends Sent to Samoan Jo's
description: The doorman checks for invitations at the entrance, insisting only card players can come in. Eddy argues, offering money instead, but the doorman allows only him to enter. The rest of the group is turned away and told to wait at Samoan Jo's, a pub nearby. Eddy hesitates, asking if Samoan Jo's is the pub, clearly uneasy about leaving his friends behind.
related_events: Doorman allows Eddy entry but denies access to his friends
Doorman enforces strict entry policy for card players only
Eddy questions the location of Samoan Jo's

name: Dean Interrupts Gary's Interrogation in the Bedroom
description: Dean walks into the large bedroom carrying an armful of rifles. Inside, Lord and Lady Appleton Smythe Winston and Daisy's parents are tied up in bed. Gary is kneeling beside them, holding a lit piece of tissue between the toes of the old man. Dean demands to know what Gary is doing. Gary replies that he's trying to find out where they keep the money. Dean scoffs, pointing out the shabby furniture and doubting the captives have any money at all. He insists they already have the guns and should move on. Suddenly, a shotgun fires. The ancient butler stumbles into the room, wielding a pair of old hammer-lock guns. The recoil knocks him off his feet. The second shot goes into the ceiling, showering him with plaster. Dean looks down at the butler, telling him to be more careful and nearly hitting Gary. The blast has torn through the center of Gary's hair, leaving two smoking tufts standing up like ears. Gary sits frozen, mouth open, unresponsive.
related_events: Dean enters bedroom with stolen rifles
Dean confronts Gary about torturing the aristocrats
Gary tortures tied-up aristocrats with burning tissue to extract information
related_occasions: Home Invasion At Appleton Smythe Winston Residence

name: The Butler's Reckless Shot
description: The ancient butler bursts into the bedroom wielding a pair of old hammer-lock guns. He fires one shot, but the recoil sends him tumbling backward, knocking him off his feet. The second shot goes wild, tearing through the ceiling and showering the room with plaster. The blast rips through the center of Gary's bouffant hairstyle, leaving behind two smoking tufts resembling ears. Gary stands frozen, mouth open, visibly shaken. Dean looks down at the fallen butler and says, 'You want to be more careful, old fella. You very nearly took my man's head clean off with that.'
related_events: Butler's shotgun misfires during confrontation, causing chaos
Dean reprimands butler for reckless gunfire
Gary suffers shock from near-miss gunshot to the head

name: Ed Heads to the Restroom, Sparking Banter Among the Lads
description: The boys sit in silence at the bar, staring straight ahead, their faces tense. Ed breaks the quiet, saying, 'I am going to the john,' and walks away. Tom turns to the others and says, 'What you telling us for?' Soap replies, 'Tom, you're all heart.' Tom ignores the jab and says, 'Listen cooky, you want to make sure that man rests before he plays; it's in all our interests.' As they speak, a beautiful girl named Daisy walks through the bar, passing by the group. The lads start to respond to JD, the bar owner, who asks how things are going, but each one stops mid-sentence, mouth open, distracted by her presence.
related_events: Ed announces he is going to the restroom
Tom expresses indifference to Ed's activities
Soap sarcastically compliments Tom
Tom insists Ed must rest before playing

name: JD Greets the Group as Daisy Enters the Bar
description: JD walks up to the bar where the lads are sitting and asks how things are going. He checks in with Soap about the cooking and then asks where his son Ed is. As he speaks, the group tries to respond but falters, their mouths hanging open. At that moment, Daisy walks through the bar, drawing every eye. The room stays still as she passes, the men silent, their attention fixed on her.
related_events: JD greets the group and inquires about Soap and Ed
Daisy enters the bar and captures the attention of the group

name: Harry and Barry Wait for Big Chris
description: In Harry's office, Harry polishes a shotgun while talking with Barry. He asks if Big Chris is on his way, and Barry says he should arrive any minute. Barry warns that sending Big Chris to retrieve a large sum of money is a mistake, saying he wouldn't trust him to bring it back. Harry continues with his task as the sound of footsteps approaches the office.
related_events: Hatchet inquires about Big Chris's arrival
Harry polishes shotgun while talking with Barry
Barry expresses distrust in Big Chris handling large sum of money

name: Plank Describes the Unlocked Gate and the People's Fear
description: Plank tells Dog that the steel gate at the location is never locked. He says he’s been there fifty times and it’s always been open, adding that the people there don’t suspect anyone. He explains that everyone who goes there is wealthy and believes in karma, thinking that if they don’t harm others, no one will harm them. Dog asks if there’s any way the people could trace things back to them. Plank says even if they could, they wouldn’t do anything because they’re too scared and weak.
related_events: Plank reveals security gate is never locked at the location
Plank dismisses possibility of retaliation from the people at the location

name: Big Chris Walks Up the Stairs and Knocks on the Door
description: Big Chris walks up the stairs. He reaches the top, steps forward, and knocks on the door.
related_events: Big Chris walks up the stairs
Big Chris knocks on the door

name: Big Chris Walks the Line
description: Big Chris climbs the stairs and stops at a door. He knocks. Below, a voice recalls how he once refused to take from the weak, how he searched the streets until he found the owner of a lost tenner. The voice speaks of his father, and his father before him, men who collected what was owed without flinching, even at death’s door. Big Chris stands in the hall, solid, watchful. He returns what isn’t his, but when provoked, he strikes—fast, hard, without warning. Those who cross him feel the weight of his rage, sudden and brutal. He walks the edge, calm one moment, a storm the next.
related_events: Big Chris refuses to steal from vulnerable individuals
Big Chris searches for lost money to return to its owner
Big Chris exhibits extreme violence due to uncontrollable temper

name: Big Chris Ascends the Stairs
description: Big Chris walks up the stairs, each step steady and deliberate. He reaches the top and stands before a door. Without hesitation, he raises his hand and knocks.

description: The Scousers arrive at the front door and unpack their lock-picking kit. They crouch near the lock, examining it closely, and begin working on it with their tools.
related_events: Scousers prepare to pick the front door lock

name: Bacon Receives a Cocktail at Samoan Jo's
description: Samoa Jo hands Bacon a large, leafy cocktail. Bacon stares at the drink, taken aback by its size and appearance. 'What's that?' he asks. Samoa Jo replies, 'A cocktail, you asked for a cocktail.' Bacon says he only wanted a refreshing drink, not something that looks like a rainforest. He asks if this is a pub. Samoa Jo tells him it's a Samoan pub. Bacon mutters that he thought it was a regular pub. Samoa Jo stands by the bar, unmoved.
related_events: Samoa Jo serves Bacon a large leafy cocktail
Bacon expresses dismay at the size of the cocktail
Bacon questions the nature of the establishment
Samoa Jo clarifies the nature of the pub

name: Bacon's Request for Lower Volume Sparks Tension
description: Bacon approaches Rory Breaker and asks him to turn the TV down. Rory takes a swig of his drink, keeps his eyes fixed on the screen, and says, 'No.' He frowns at Bacon, who returns the glare. Soap then remarks, 'This is the English-Brazil game, isn't it?'
related_events: Bacon requests Rory Breaker to lower the TV volume
Rory Breaker refuses Bacon's request and displays hostility
Bacon exchanges a hostile glance with Rory Breaker
Soap identifies the TV broadcast as the English-Brazil game

name: Eddy Arrives at the Boxing Gym
description: Eddy walks into the boxing gym alone and pauses, taking in the scene. The usual space is transformed, with people sitting around counting money and exchanging it for chips. He moves to the only empty chair and sits down, glancing quickly around, especially behind him. He raises his eyebrows, then says he would have brought his gloves if he’d known. A man named Hatchet approaches and greets him as JD's son. Eddy confirms his identity and offers an apology for not knowing the man’s father. Hatchet replies that Eddy might meet him if he keeps going the way he is. Nearby, an attractive blonde croupier shuffles a deck of cards. Eddy turns to her and says, 'Evening Tanya, it has been a while.'
related_events: Eddy enters the boxing gym alone and observes the surroundings
Eddy expresses surprise about not bringing gloves

name: Eddy Arrives at the Boxing Gym
description: Eddy enters the boxing gym and looks around, noticing everyone seated and counting money, converting it into chips. He takes the only empty chair and glances behind him. Phil and Don respond to his raised eyebrows and comment about the situation being dramatic by explaining it's for security. Eddy says he would have brought his gloves if he had known.
related_events: Phil and Don explain the security reason for the gathering
related_occasions: Boxing Gym Gathering With Security Measures

name: Hatchet Greets Eddy and Warns of Consequences
description: Eddy enters the boxing gym and takes the only empty chair, glancing around, especially behind him. The others are seated, counting money and exchanging it for chips. name: Eddy Greets Tanya at the Boxing Gym

related_occasions: Boxing Gym Gathering With Security Measures

name: Gary and Dean Meet Barry at the Strip Club
description: Gary and Dean, two men in their late twenties with strong Liverpudlian accents, meet Barry at a strip club where scantily clad women dance around blue poles. Barry tells them to break into a stately home and take all the guns from inside a gun cabinet, promising payment when they deliver. He tells them they can keep anything outside the cabinet. Gary responds sarcastically, saying they’d better find something worth taking. Barry says if it looks old, it’s valuable, and tells them to stop complaining. Gary asks who they’re really working for, and Barry warns him not to ask too many questions. After checking his watch, Barry says he’s leaving and tells them to call when the job is done. As he walks away, Gary mutters that he hates southerners. Barry, under his breath, calls them northern monkeys and exits.
related_events: Gary and Dean meet Barry at a strip club
Barry assigns a theft task to Gary and Dean

name: Gary and Dean Question the Job at the Strip Club
description: Gary and Dean stand in the dim light of the strip club, watching as near-naked girls dance around blue poles. Barry approaches, speaking sharply. Gary asks about shotguns, wondering if they mean guns that fire shot. Barry mocks him, confirming it and instructing them to take everything from inside the gun cabinet. He tells them he’ll pay upon delivery and that anything outside the cabinet is theirs to keep. Gary mutters sarcastically, unimpressed. Barry assures them there will be valuables in the stately home. Dean asks what kind, and Barry says antiques. Dean protests, saying they don’t know anything about antiques—they usually rob post offices and steal cars. Barry cuts him off, saying if something looks old, it’s worth money, and tells them to stop complaining and do the job. Gary asks who’s really behind the job, but Barry warns him not to push. Gary compares it to a James Bond film, earning a sharp reminder from Barry about who’s giving the orders. Barry checks his watch, says he’s leaving, and tells them to call when it’s done. As he walks away, Gary mutters to Dean that he hates Southern men. Barry, already stepping out, whispers under his breath about hating Northern thugs.
related_events: Barry clarifies the theft target as antiques
Gary questions the authority behind the theft job

name: Barry Leaves the Strip Club After Tense Meeting
description: Barry checks his watch and announces he is leaving, telling Gary and Dean the job is theirs to carry out. Before walking away, he warns Gary not to question him, reminding him that he only knows what he needs to know. As Barry exits, he mutters under his breath, calling Gary and Dean 'fucking Northern monkeys.' The two men watch him leave with clear disgust. Gary, once Barry is out of earshot, remarks that he hates 'these Southern shites.'
related_events: Barry asserts control over information and departs
Barry mutters derogatory remark about Gary and Dean
Gary expresses disdain for Barry after his departure

name: Hatchet Clears the Desk and Begins the Meeting
